prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: Keeping it simple and light on us so that we could easily remember by the shapes and the colors of the Legos. We both gave input as to what we thought the shapes looked like. We did not change our strategy, I basically called the shapes and she agreed and sometimes she called the shapes something and we would agree and she would type in the box while we were discussing what we wanted to call the parts. It went quite well, we were pretty much in agreement on everything...basically the same type of strategy.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: none

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: We both suggested names at times, we used things that were relatively easy and relatable, we took turns and she would type the names in the box while we were discussing and I was mostly coming up with the name of the images and shapes but she did share input when needed. I think we shared responsibility equally, we seemed to be on the same page.

prompt_strategy.value: At the start, we used the eyes and the direction that they were pointing.   Then you started to mix in the googly eyes which then we turned to the colour of the hat then the colour of the arms and feet.   this worked great on the 4th round you changed and added shapes. We tried to incorporate this however, we ran out of time so some of them we had to guess that are team member was doing the same on shape or size.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake

# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?

prompt_strategy.value: Often it was easiest to use names which reflected items which we were familiar with, and which we felt the items looked like. The items had eyes, so often we personified them, personified them, sometimes giving them names. There were some slight cultural and perspective differences but we were able to overcome these and reach a middle ground through thorough discussion. After we had named them, we each took time to repeat the names out loud in order to ensure that we had remembered one time, my partner had hesitated when remembering a name, so I had suggested that we could change it if they prefer. They decided not to.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: I do not think I made any mistakes. Either myself or my partner it seems had submitted one of the names prematurely so that only the first two letters were included in the answer. This was the only mistake made between us throughout the experiment.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: We did not have a structured approach. If one of us felt particularly strongly about a word, we would suggest it, and the other participant would have room to either agree or to disagree. More often than not, we agreed on what to call the items, or what their distinguishing characteristics were. It seemed that there was quite an even division when naming them, but this came about naturally through a balanced discussion.
